answer: Each identity must lock a 500-token bond and present a one-per-hardware credential tied to a fused chip serial, so one device yields one registry entry. A fake identity locks 500 tokens for 30 epochs, forfeiting 80 percent on detection, with each duplicate flagged by an independent echo of the registration pulse. Splitting identities raises marginal cost per copy, and a shared slashing penalty on the hardware knoll removes any gain from duplication.
